newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Bank of Baroda cuts prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: India's Bank of Baroda cuts prime lending rate.

text.p: The state-owned Bank of Baroda said on Thursday it has decided to cut its prime lending rate to 15.5 percent per annum from 16 percent effective October 1.
Chairman and managing director K. Kannan said the bank is also cutting interest rates on deposits held by expatriate Indians.

Deposits under the non-resident non-repatriable rupee deposit scheme (NRNR) would now attract 16 percent per annum against 17 percent, while non-resident external accounts would receive 14 percent against 15 percent, he told Reuters.
The new rates are effective October 1.
Kannan said there was no change in interest rates on domestic deposits for the time being.
"We will decide after the busy season credit policy is released next month," he said.
The State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial bank, earlier this month cut its prime lending rate to 15.5 percent per annum from 16 percent.
Other state-run banks are expected to announce similar cuts, analysts say.
The Bank of Baroda plans to issue one billion 10-rupee face value shares at a premium of 75-80 rupees.
"We are likely to come out with a public offering of equity towards the end of November or the beginning of December," Kannan said.
